title: Fish Pathology & Parasitology
source_note: Standard NUC-aligned Nigerian university 300L Fish Pathology & Parasitology curriculum: causes and types of fish disease (bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic, nutritional, environmental), common fish pathogens and parasites in Nigerian aquaculture, clinical signs and diagnosis, disease-stress relationships, biosecurity, and treatment/prevention principles. Kept distinct from Fish Physiology (FIS301) by focusing on abnormal/disease states rather than normal function.

questions.question: Fish diseases are generally classified by cause into which broad categories?
options: Infectious (bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic) and non-infectious (nutritional, environmental, genetic)
Only bacterial and viral
Only diseases caused by poor water quality
Only hereditary diseases
questions.correct_answer: Infectious (bacterial, viral, fungal, parasitic) and non-infectious (nutritional, environmental, genetic)
questions.explanation: Fish diseases are broadly grouped into infectious diseases caused by pathogens and non-infectious diseases arising from nutritional deficiencies, poor environment, or genetic factors.

questions.question: Aeromonas hydrophila, a common bacterial pathogen in Nigerian aquaculture, typically causes:
options: Motile Aeromonas septicemia (MAS) with skin ulcers and hemorrhages
White spot disease on the skin
Swim bladder gas over-inflation
Improved growth rate in infected fish
questions.correct_answer: Motile Aeromonas septicemia (MAS) with skin ulcers and hemorrhages
questions.explanation: Aeromonas hydrophila is an opportunistic bacterium causing motile Aeromonas septicemia, characterized by hemorrhagic septicemia, skin ulcers, and fin/tail rot, especially under stress.

questions.question: Columnaris disease in cultured fish is caused by which type of pathogen?
options: A bacterium (Flavobacterium columnare)
A virus
A protozoan parasite
A helminth worm
questions.correct_answer: A bacterium (Flavobacterium columnare)
questions.explanation: Columnaris disease is caused by the bacterium Flavobacterium columnare, producing characteristic saddleback lesions and gill/skin erosion, often linked to stress and poor water quality.

questions.question: Bacterial fin and tail rot in pond-cultured fish is most commonly associated with:
options: Poor water quality and overcrowding predisposing fish to opportunistic bacteria
A virus transmitted only through the air
A nutritional excess of vitamin C
Genetic mutation with no environmental link
questions.correct_answer: Poor water quality and overcrowding predisposing fish to opportunistic bacteria
questions.explanation: Fin and tail rot is typically an opportunistic bacterial infection that develops when fish are stressed by poor water quality, overcrowding, or physical injury.

questions.question: Ichthyophthirius multifiliis, the causative agent of 'Ich' or white spot disease, is classified as a:
options: Ciliated protozoan parasite
Bacterium
Virus
Trematode worm
questions.correct_answer: Ciliated protozoan parasite
questions.explanation: Ich (white spot disease) is caused by Ichthyophthirius multifiliis, a ciliated protozoan that burrows into the skin and gills, producing visible white cysts.

questions.question: Which clinical sign is most characteristic of an Ichthyophthirius (white spot / Ich) infection?
options: Small white nodules scattered over the skin, fins, and gills
Complete loss of the swim bladder
Bright red gill filaments only
Excessive fat deposition in the liver
questions.correct_answer: Small white nodules scattered over the skin, fins, and gills
questions.explanation: Ich infection is diagnosed by the presence of tiny white cyst-like nodules ('white spots') on the skin, fins, and gills caused by the parasite embedding in the epidermis.

questions.question: Lernaea (the 'anchor worm') is a parasite of fish that is classified as a:
options: Parasitic copepod crustacean
Bacterium
Fungus
Protozoan
questions.correct_answer: Parasitic copepod crustacean
questions.explanation: Lernaea species are copepod crustaceans that attach to the fish's body with an anchor-like holdfast, causing localized inflammation and secondary infection.

questions.question: Argulus, commonly known as the 'fish louse,' primarily damages fish by:
options: Attaching to the skin and piercing it to feed on blood and tissue fluid
Living exclusively inside the fish's gut without attaching externally
Producing toxins that only affect eggs
Growing inside the swim bladder
questions.correct_answer: Attaching to the skin and piercing it to feed on blood and tissue fluid
questions.explanation: Argulus is an ectoparasitic branchiuran crustacean that attaches to the skin, piercing it with a stylet to feed on blood, causing irritation, lesions, and entry points for secondary infection.

questions.question: Monogenean parasites (e.g., Dactylogyrus and Gyrodactylus) primarily infest which fish organs?
options: Gills and skin
Only the liver
Only the swim bladder
Only the brain
questions.correct_answer: Gills and skin
questions.explanation: Monogenean flatworms such as Dactylogyrus (gill flukes) and Gyrodactylus (skin flukes) attach to and feed on the gills or skin, causing irritation, excess mucus, and respiratory distress.

questions.question: Saprolegnia, a common fungal pathogen in fish and fish eggs, typically appears as:
options: Cotton-like white or grayish growth on the skin, fins, or egg surface
Bright red pinpoint spots
A hard calcified shell over the body
Small black dots under the scales only
questions.correct_answer: Cotton-like white or grayish growth on the skin, fins, or egg surface
questions.explanation: Saprolegniasis presents as a characteristic cotton-wool-like fungal growth, commonly affecting damaged skin, fins, or unfertilized/dead eggs in hatcheries.

questions.question: Fungal infections such as Saprolegnia in fish are most often described as:
options: Secondary/opportunistic, exploiting fish already stressed, injured, or with weakened immunity
Always the primary cause of fish death regardless of fish condition
Impossible to occur in fish eggs
Beneficial to fish health
questions.correct_answer: Secondary/opportunistic, exploiting fish already stressed, injured, or with weakened immunity
questions.explanation: Saprolegnia and related water molds are typically opportunistic, invading tissue already compromised by injury, stress, poor water quality, or another primary infection.

questions.question: Viral hemorrhagic septicemia and other fish viral diseases are generally difficult to treat because:
options: There is no effective direct antiviral treatment, so prevention and biosecurity are the main control measures
Antibiotics reliably cure all fish viral infections
Viruses cannot infect fish at all
Viral diseases never cause economic losses in aquaculture
questions.correct_answer: There is no effective direct antiviral treatment, so prevention and biosecurity are the main control measures
questions.explanation: As with most viral diseases, there is generally no curative antiviral drug for fish, making prevention, biosecurity, and management of stress the primary control strategies.

questions.question: Endoparasites, as distinct from ectoparasites, are defined as parasites that:
options: Live inside the host's body, such as in the gut or organs
Live only on the outer surface of the host
Are always visible without dissection
Cannot cause any harm to the host
questions.correct_answer: Live inside the host's body, such as in the gut or organs
questions.explanation: Endoparasites reside internally within host tissues or organs (e.g., intestinal helminths), while ectoparasites live on external surfaces such as skin and gills.

questions.question: Digenean trematodes commonly encountered in fish typically require which type of life cycle?
options: An indirect life cycle involving one or more intermediate hosts
A direct life cycle with no intermediate host at all
A life cycle entirely outside water
Reproduction only within another fish of the same species
questions.correct_answer: An indirect life cycle involving one or more intermediate hosts
questions.explanation: Digenean trematodes typically have complex, indirect life cycles involving intermediate hosts such as snails and sometimes a second intermediate host before reaching the fish (definitive or intermediate) host.

questions.question: In fish disease diagnosis, a wet mount skin/gill scrape examined under a microscope is used mainly to detect:
options: External protozoan and monogenean parasites
Internal bacterial septicemia only
Genetic mutations
Water pH levels
questions.correct_answer: External protozoan and monogenean parasites
questions.explanation: A fresh wet mount of skin or gill mucus/tissue allows direct microscopic visualization of external parasites such as Ichthyophthirius, Trichodina, and monogenean flukes.

questions.question: Bacterial culture and sensitivity testing in fish disease diagnosis is primarily used to:
options: Identify the causative bacterium and determine which antibiotics are effective against it
Measure the water's dissolved oxygen level
Determine the fish's exact age
Assess the taste quality of the fish flesh
questions.correct_answer: Identify the causative bacterium and determine which antibiotics are effective against it
questions.explanation: Culturing a bacterial isolate followed by antibiotic sensitivity testing identifies the pathogen and guides selection of an effective, targeted treatment.

questions.question: The relationship between environmental stress and disease outbreaks in cultured fish is best described as:
options: Stress suppresses immune function, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic pathogens
Stress has no influence on disease occurrence
Stress always cures existing infections
Stress only affects fish growth, never disease resistance
questions.correct_answer: Stress suppresses immune function, increasing susceptibility to opportunistic pathogens
questions.explanation: Chronic stress (e.g., poor water quality, overcrowding, handling) elevates cortisol and suppresses immune defenses, making fish more vulnerable to opportunistic bacterial, fungal, and parasitic infections.

questions.question: Poor water quality, such as elevated ammonia, is a significant concern in fish pathology because it:
options: Damages gill tissue and stresses fish, predisposing them to infectious disease
Has no effect on disease susceptibility
Directly kills all bacterial pathogens in the pond
Improves the fish's immune response
questions.correct_answer: Damages gill tissue and stresses fish, predisposing them to infectious disease
questions.explanation: Elevated ammonia and other water quality stressors damage gill epithelium and weaken the fish's physiological condition, creating openings for opportunistic pathogens.

questions.question: Quarantine of newly introduced fish stock before adding them to an existing population is a key biosecurity practice because it:
options: Allows time to observe and screen for disease before exposing the resident population
Is required only for ornamental fish, never for food fish
Guarantees the new stock will grow faster
Eliminates the need for any further disease monitoring
questions.correct_answer: Allows time to observe and screen for disease before exposing the resident population
questions.explanation: Quarantine isolates newly introduced fish for observation, allowing detection and treatment of latent infections before they can be introduced to the main population.

questions.question: Formalin is commonly used in aquaculture disease management mainly as a:
options: External parasiticide/disinfectant bath treatment
Oral antibiotic administered in feed only
Growth-promoting hormone
Water pH buffer
questions.correct_answer: External parasiticide/disinfectant bath treatment
questions.explanation: Formalin is widely used as a bath treatment to control external protozoan and monogenean parasites and to disinfect eggs and equipment, but it is not an antibiotic.

questions.question: The indiscriminate use of antibiotics in aquaculture is discouraged primarily because it can lead to:
options: Development of antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains
Immediate improvement in fish flavor
Complete elimination of all fish diseases permanently
Lower production costs with no drawbacks
questions.correct_answer: Development of antibiotic-resistant bacterial strains
questions.explanation: Overuse or misuse of antibiotics promotes selection for resistant bacterial populations, reducing future treatment effectiveness and posing broader public health concerns.

questions.question: Proper pond preparation, including drying and liming between production cycles, helps prevent disease by:
options: Reducing pathogen and parasite loads that persist in pond sediment
Increasing the concentration of ammonia in the water
Encouraging fungal growth on pond walls
Having no effect on subsequent fish health
questions.correct_answer: Reducing pathogen and parasite loads that persist in pond sediment
questions.explanation: Drying and liming ponds between cycles helps kill resting stages of parasites and pathogens in the sediment, lowering disease risk in the next production cycle.

questions.question: Trichodina, a common ectoparasite of cultured fish, is classified as a:
options: Ciliated protozoan
Trematode
Cestode (tapeworm)
Nematode
questions.correct_answer: Ciliated protozoan
questions.explanation: Trichodina is a disc-shaped, ciliated protozoan ectoparasite that moves and attaches to the skin and gills using a ring of denticles, often associated with poor water quality.

questions.question: Exophthalmia (pop-eye) observed in diseased fish is generally a clinical sign associated with:
options: Systemic infection or fluid accumulation behind the eye
A completely healthy, well-fed fish
Normal aging with no disease significance
Excess dietary vitamin A only
questions.correct_answer: Systemic infection or fluid accumulation behind the eye
questions.explanation: Exophthalmia (bulging eyes) is a common clinical sign in fish with systemic bacterial or viral infections, often accompanied by fluid buildup behind the eye.

questions.question: A necropsy (post-mortem examination) in fish disease diagnosis is performed mainly to:
options: Examine internal organs for lesions, abnormalities, or the presence of parasites/pathogens
Measure the fish's swimming speed before death
Determine the exact water temperature at time of death
Assess the fish's market price
questions.correct_answer: Examine internal organs for lesions, abnormalities, or the presence of parasites/pathogens
questions.explanation: Necropsy involves dissecting a dead or moribund fish to inspect internal organs for gross lesions, abnormal fluid, or parasites, aiding disease diagnosis.

questions.question: Nutritional diseases in cultured fish, such as those caused by vitamin C deficiency, typically result in:
options: Impaired collagen formation, leading to skeletal deformities and poor wound healing
Immediate death within hours regardless of severity
Enhanced disease resistance
No observable clinical signs at all
questions.correct_answer: Impaired collagen formation, leading to skeletal deformities and poor wound healing
questions.explanation: Vitamin C is essential for collagen synthesis in fish; deficiency causes conditions such as scoliosis, lordosis, and poor wound healing, since most fish cannot synthesize their own vitamin C.

questions.question: Gas bubble disease in fish is primarily caused by:
options: Supersaturation of dissolved gases in the water
A bacterial infection of the gills
A parasitic infestation of the swim bladder
Dietary protein deficiency
questions.correct_answer: Supersaturation of dissolved gases in the water
questions.explanation: Gas bubble disease results from fish being exposed to water supersaturated with dissolved gases (often nitrogen), causing bubbles to form in blood vessels and tissues, an environmental rather than infectious disease.

questions.question: Zoonotic potential in fish pathology refers to the possibility that:
options: Certain fish pathogens or parasites can be transmitted to and cause disease in humans
Fish diseases can spread to plants
Human diseases can never affect fish
All fish pathogens are exclusively species-specific with zero human risk
questions.correct_answer: Certain fish pathogens or parasites can be transmitted to and cause disease in humans
questions.explanation: Some fish-associated organisms (e.g., certain bacteria, or parasites transmitted via undercooked fish) have zoonotic potential, meaning they can cause disease in humans, which is a food-safety concern in fisheries.

questions.question: Histopathology, as a diagnostic tool in fish pathology, involves:
options: Microscopic examination of stained tissue sections to detect cellular-level damage or pathogens
Measuring the fish's total body length only
Testing water samples for pH alone
Weighing the fish before and after feeding
questions.correct_answer: Microscopic examination of stained tissue sections to detect cellular-level damage or pathogens
questions.explanation: Histopathology examines thin, stained sections of fish tissue under a microscope to identify cellular changes, inflammation, or pathogens not visible by gross examination alone.

questions.question: Overcrowding in a fish pond or tank increases disease risk mainly because it:
options: Raises stress levels and facilitates faster pathogen and parasite transmission between fish
Automatically improves water quality
Reduces contact between fish, lowering transmission
Has no relationship to disease spread
questions.correct_answer: Raises stress levels and facilitates faster pathogen and parasite transmission between fish
questions.explanation: High stocking density increases physiological stress and close contact among fish, both of which accelerate the spread of contagious pathogens and parasites.

questions.question: Which of the following best describes an 'epizootic' in fish health terminology?
options: An outbreak of disease affecting many fish in a population at the same time
A single fish with a chronic, non-contagious illness
A disease found only in one isolated fish species worldwide
A term unrelated to disease, referring to fish migration
questions.correct_answer: An outbreak of disease affecting many fish in a population at the same time
questions.explanation: An epizootic is the animal-health equivalent of an epidemic: a disease outbreak affecting a large number of animals (here, fish) in a population simultaneously.

questions.question: Disinfection of hatchery equipment and eggs is an important disease prevention measure because it:
options: Reduces the load of pathogens (e.g., fungal spores, bacteria) that could infect eggs and larvae
Is unnecessary since fish eggs cannot be infected
Increases hatching failure rates deliberately
Replaces the need for good water quality management
questions.correct_answer: Reduces the load of pathogens (e.g., fungal spores, bacteria) that could infect eggs and larvae
questions.explanation: Eggs and larvae are especially vulnerable to fungal and bacterial infection; disinfecting equipment and eggs (e.g., with iodine solutions) reduces pathogen exposure during this sensitive stage.
